﻿* Solar Thermal
Solar thermal systems use sunlight to produce useful heat. Solar collectors absorb or concentrate solar radiation and transfer the heat to water, steam, thermal oil, or another heat-transfer fluid. Unlike an electric or fuel-fired boiler, the main energy input is solar energy, so there is no direct combustion at the collector.
Field
	Value
	Process
	Hot-water generation, steam generation, pasteurization, drying, washing, sterilizing, cooking, pre-heating and other industrial process-heat applications
	Temperature
	~80–100°C with Flat Plate Collectors → ~150–200°C with Evacuated Tube Collectors → ~150–450°C with concentrating systems such as Parabolic Trough/Linear Fresnel; advanced systems can reach higher temperatures
	Energy source
	Solar radiation; small amounts of electricity may be required for pumps, controls and tracking systems
	Efficiency
	Typically ~40–70% thermal efficiency, depending on collector technology, operating temperature and solar conditions
	CAPEX
	Highly technology- and size-dependent. Low-temperature FPC/ETC systems: roughly ₹10,000–₹40,000/m² as a broad planning range; larger concentrating industrial systems can be substantially more expensive and should be estimated in ₹/kW or ₹/m² for the specific technology and capacity
	OPEX
	Low–Medium — mainly collector/mirror cleaning, pump and valve maintenance, piping, controls and, for concentrating systems, tracking/heat-transfer-fluid maintenance
	Lifetime
	Typically 15–30 years, depending on technology; FPC ~20–25 years, ETC ~15–20 years and concentrating systems commonly ~20–30 years
	Space
	Requires a shadow-free roof or ground area. FPC/ETC can be roof-mounted; concentrating systems generally require a larger open solar field
	Constraints
	Solar availability, cloudy/rainy weather, night-time operation, dust/soiling, shading, available roof/land area, required process temperature and need for backup during low-solar periods
